extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism/adjudication summary for final artifacts; this does not convert the paper into AMP antimicrobial/anticancer evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: m9R-conjugated Cas9 plus sgRNA complexed with 9R enabled CPP-mediated RGEN delivery and target DNA cleavage/gene disruption in human cells.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Human cell-based episomal reporter assay; xml:sec=Endogenous gene disruption; xml:fig=3; xml:fig=4

mechanism_claims.limitations: Functional evidence is genome-editing delivery, not antimicrobial or anticancer AMP activity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The 9R CPP condensed sgRNA into positively charged nanoparticles, supported by gel shift, EtBr exclusion, DLS/zeta-potential, and SEM evidence.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Physicochemical delivery evidence does not establish antimicrobial/anticancer activity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CPP-mediated direct RGEN delivery was reported with reduced off-target mutation frequencies relative to plasmid transfection under the tested conditions.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Reduced off-target cleavage effects of Cas9-m9R and sgRNA:9R; xml:fig=7:Figure 7

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper cautions that exact quantitative comparison to plasmid delivery is difficult because RGEN concentrations differ between delivery methods.
